newsitem.title: CANADA: CAW's Hargrove says family received bomb threat.
newsitem.headline: CAW's Hargrove says family received bomb threat.

text.p: Canadian Auto Workers President Buzz Hargrove said on Thursday that his former wife and his family have received a bomb scare and other threats from people angry over the talks with Canadian Airlines Corp.

Hargrove told a news conference that someone published his ex wife's telephone number on the Internet which resulted in a slew of ugly phone calls overnight and during the day, including the bomb threat.
He said on Thursday someone also slashed the tires of a car belonging to the family which lives in the Toronto area.
"It's really taken quite a toll on my ability to concentrate on this," said the 52-year-old Hargrove.

The Canadian Auto Workers are in a white knuckle set of negotiations trying to resist wage roll backs with money-losing Canadian Airlines. The union, which represents ticket agents, is the only one of the six unions to reject wage cuts the company said it needed to survive.
Hargrove said the police have been notified and he was now looking into extra security for his family. He said he was considering moving them to somewhere safe while the talks continued.
But Hargrove said he was not concerned about his own safety. "I'm at a stage in my life where nothing much scares me," he said.
